images.caption: The beginning of the city of Yelisavetgrad (Kropyvnytskyi) was the construction in 1754 on the right bank of the Ingul river a fortress, named after St. righteous Elisabeth, the mother of John the Baptist. Inside it are two large cemeteries - the Pantheon of Eternal Glory, dedicated to soldiers who fell in World War II, a cemetery of 50,000 civilians, mostly Jews, killed during the Nazi occupation, and one of the city's hospitals.
images.alt: The beginning of the city of Yelisavetgrad (Kropyvnytskyi) was the construction in 1754 on the right bank of the Ingul river a fortress, named after St. righteous Elisabeth, the mother of John the Baptist. Inside it are two large cemeteries - the Pantheon of Eternal Glory, dedicated to soldiers who fell in World War II, a cemetery of 50,000 civilians, mostly Jews, killed during the Nazi occupation, and one of the city's hospitals.
